title: Joining the Ninth Ward parade band under Gilbert and Martinez
summary: Sonny Henry recommended him to the band; Gilbert tested players with sight music, Martinez took over, and he describes a rehearsal and the tune Delia.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Who was the leader, the boss of the whole band?

A fellow by the name of Mr. Gilbert, you know. He had it in charge, so he said he's going to run a test. He run a test. He was going to run a test. And put the music up, you know. And the music wasn't all that hard. And a whole lot of fellows couldn't make, didn't know nothing at all. And a week or so they cut the band down to about 70-something. They stayed in on trombone. Frankie Duesen still there? They passed him some kind of way they liked him, you know. Then again, Frankie Bluffey, if he hear something once, you got it, Jerry.
And they got a, my dad didn't know what he was doing.

He was going to be a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a band. And then they got a, my dad's man, by the name of old man Martinez, he took the band over after he got a, and Gilbert, before he left, he bought a whole lot of orchestration. You know, you want to set up band with that. So they had the same Sonny Henry playing the trombone. And they practiced and practiced and practiced. So they asked me to play one day. I don't know if Sonny wasn't there. And now I take them, play the trombone and pieces and I went right along with them, with the pieces, you know. So I had been playing, I had been playing the local show and all them, all them places that I got that, that music was, I was, you, you, you be sharp when you, when you keep up there, you're, it's nothing, nothing, actually you're, it's nowhere. So when I went there, they told me that, they kept me on the trombone. And we had an orchestra and a march band, you see, the concert band. And we played with them and again what you call a layout, you see, dance like, and, well, they had, they're taking two bands and they had another bunch, they had an orchestra and we would take two and playing. And we had a piece, we had practice and they didn't know we had practice. I think I was a camellia, uh, what's up, Amelia, I don't care what it is, Cecilia, something like that. I don't know, I don't know.
What's the name, but the name's not again?

Yeah, so we had that. Delia. And late at night, the fella that we was playing, we put that up, you know, and we played that number. It ain't so easy neither when you get rid of honey, no. We played that number and, and why did y'all get that from, why did y'all get that piece from? We had been rehearsed in the dance, it was a nice dance number. But you got to know your business on them numbers. And they played some nice numbers too, you know, and they got mixed up on a number, they were trying to play a jazz number, you know, and the fella had been drinking and he picked it up in the wrong key. And I tell you, that was a mess. That was a, that was a really mess.
What was the name of Vanneken?
What was the name? What was the name of that tool again? How do you spell that? Delia. Yeah.
That's a nice number. I don't know. I don't know. Oh yeah.
Well it was very popular. I'll get you the music sometime. He brought up plenty of popular numbers, you know.
And we came up with that and we did.
